Pack heat, the only advice you need. Good luck!

Youtuber Sargon of Akkad had a pretty good live stream with one. Key points are to keep calm most or all of the time and know your stats. He also does a thing where he will go back to common touchstones so things stay kinda chill and don't spiral into a shouting match. Good luck!

(Edit): Really focus on emotional appeals over statistics. People won't hear statistics by themselves. Use statistics in moderation to highlight your emotional argument.

If you go into a debate without understanding multiple viewpoints - especially those that run counter to your own - you are going to be very disappointed in your performance and the fact that most that witness that debate will easily recognize your ignorance of the topic.

TL;DR: it's not going to go well for you if you don't understand multiple viewpoints

Know who you are trying to convince. Are you trying to convince the person you are debating or the people watching? You will know early on if you can convince the person you are debating or not. If they appear to be emotionally attached to the cause, there isn't much you can do to convince them other than to place little seeds of doubt and hope they figure it out on their own.

Now, if you are trying to convince the viewers, present facts and stats and demand the same from the debaters. If they insist on only using feelings and personal thoughts, point out how those can be blinded by emotions and show data to back that up. To convince the viewer you need to make the person you are debating appear to be illogical, wrong, ill informed, and not prepared.
